title: Analyzing and Graphing Algebraic Combinations of f(x) = sqrt(x) and g(x) = sqrt(1 - x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider the functions f(x) = sqrt(x) and g(x) = sqrt(1 - x). Find the formulas, domains, ranges, and key graphical features of their: (a) sum f + g, (b) product f * g, (c) two differences f - g and g - f, and (d) two quotients f / g and g / f.

steps.title: Determine the Individual and Common Domains
steps.explanation: f(x) = sqrt(x) requires x >= 0 and g(x) = sqrt(1 - x) requires 1 - x >= 0 (x <= 1). Their intersection is the closed interval [0, 1].
steps.why: All sums, differences, and products of f and g have natural domain D_f cap D_g = [0, 1].

steps.title: Analyze the Sum (a) and Product (b) on [0, 1]
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} \text{(a) } (f + g)(x) &= \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{1 - x}, & D &= [0, 1], & R &= [1, \sqrt{2}] \\ \text{(b) } (f \cdot g)(x) &= \sqrt{x(1 - x)}, & D &= [0, 1], & R &= [0, 1/2] \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: Both f + g and f * g are symmetric about x = 1/2. The sum equals 1 at x = 0 and x = 1 and peaks at x = 1/2 with value sqrt(1/2) + sqrt(1/2) = sqrt(2). The product y = sqrt(x - x^2) satisfies (x - 1/2)^2 + y^2 = (1/2)^2 (y >= 0), which is an upper semicircle of radius 1/2 centered at (1/2, 0) with maximum 1/2 at x = 1/2.
steps.why: Completing the square x(1 - x) = 1/4 - (x - 1/2)^2 identifies the product graph as a semicircle.

steps.title: Analyze the Two Differences in Part (c)
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} (f - g)(x) &= \sqrt{x} - \sqrt{1 - x}, & D &= [0, 1], & R &= [-1, 1] \\ (g - f)(x) &= \sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{x}, & D &= [0, 1], & R &= [-1, 1] \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: On [0, 1], f - g is strictly increasing from -1 (at x = 0) through 0 (at x = 1/2) to +1 (at x = 1). Its negation g - f = -(f - g) is the reflection of f - g across the x-axis, strictly decreasing from +1 to -1.
steps.why: Since sqrt(x) increases and -sqrt(1 - x) increases on [0, 1], their sum sqrt(x) - sqrt(1 - x) is strictly increasing.

steps.title: Analyze the Two Quotients in Part (d)
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} (f/g)(x) &= \sqrt{\frac{x}{1 - x}}, & D_{f/g} &= [0, 1), & R_{f/g} &= [0, \infty) \\ (g/f)(x) &= \sqrt{\frac{1 - x}{x}}, & D_{g/f} &= (0, 1], & R_{g/f} &= [0, \infty) \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: For f/g, exclude x = 1 where g(1) = 0; the graph starts at (0, 0), passes through (1/2, 1), and has a vertical asymptote at x = 1^-. For g/f, exclude x = 0 where f(0) = 0; the graph has a vertical asymptote at x = 0^+, passes through (1/2, 1), and ends at (1, 0).
steps.why: Quotient domains exclude points where the denominator vanishes, creating vertical asymptotes at those boundary points.
